The '''1970–71 Bundesliga''' was the eighth season of the [[Bundesliga]], [[West Germany]]'s premier football league. It began on 15 August 1970 and ended on 5 June 1971.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=331262 |title=Archive 1970/1971 Schedule |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608081016/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=331262 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> [[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the two teams with the fewest points were relegated to their respective [[Regionalliga#1963–1974|Regionalliga]] divisions.

==Team changes to 1969–70==
[[TSV 1860 Munich]] and [[Alemannia Aachen]] were relegated to the [[Regionalliga#1963–1974|Regionalliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[Arminia Bielefeld]] and [[Kickers Offenbach]], who won their respective promotion play-off groups.

==Season overview==
[[Borussia Mönchengladbach]] successfully defended their title. [[FC Bayern Munich]] ended up in second place, but not without a title, as they defeated [[1. FC Köln]] in the [[1971–72 DFB-Pokal|domestic cup]] final, thereby qualifying for the [[1971–72 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]]. As a consequence, Bayern's original spot in the newly formed [[1971–72 UEFA Cup|UEFA Cup]], to which teams finishing in second to fifth place were permitted to enter, went to Köln. The latter were joined by [[Hertha BSC]], [[Eintracht Braunschweig]] and [[Hamburger SV]]. The teams demoted to the [[Regionalliga#1963–1974|Regionalliga]] were [[Kickers Offenbach]] and [[Rot-Weiss Essen]].

===Bundesliga scandal===
{{main|Bundesliga scandal (1971)}}
Eventually, it was revealed that the decisions in the league had not been determined on the strength of each team alone. On 6 June 1971, Offenbach chairman [[Horst-Gregorio Canellas]] played an audio tape to an audience who originally had gathered to celebrate Canellas' 50th birthday. The circle included national team coach [[Helmut Schön]], as well as high [[German Football Association|DFB]] representatives and also a few reporters. The tape proved that matches had been sold for money. Soon, the DFB launched its own investigation. It was discovered that a total of 18 games had been fixed, including almost every relevant match in the relegation decision. Over 60 players from ten clubs were involved and nearly one million [[Deutsche Mark|marks]] had been paid. Nevertheless, the first verdicts were not spoken until after the start of the following season, meaning that the bribed games officially counted in the final table.<ref name="bundesligaScandal">{{cite web |url=http://www.planet-wissen.de/pw/Artikel,,,,,,,EE97460B1A0A1E46E0340003BA5E0905,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,.html |title=Der Bundesliga-Skandal 1971 |last=Kracht |first=Claudia |date=15 January 2008 |publisher=Planet Wissen |language=de |access-date=10 December 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090208105834/http://planet-wissen.de/pw/Artikel,,,,,,,EE97460B1A0A1E46E0340003BA5E0905,,,,,,,,,,,,,,,.html |archive-date=8 February 2009 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
